---
title: "About these guides"
---

## What they are

Open, step-by-step guides for analysing five common kinds of functional genomics data (bulk
RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, Hi-C and single-cell RNA-seq), from raw reads to biological
interpretation. Each guide pairs a reusable processing pipeline with worked R code, explains why
each step is done the way it is, and states plainly what the results can and cannot show. An
extension in every guide, and a shared appendix, cover comparisons across species.

## How they were checked

- **R code:** every R block was executed with R 4.5 and Bioconductor 3.22 on public example data
  (airway, PBMC 3k, DiffBind's tamoxifen set) or on synthetic files in the exact formats the
  pipelines write. The package versions are pinned in
  [`pipelines/envs/r_analysis.yaml`](https://github.com/Delta-43/comparative-genomics-guides/blob/main/pipelines/envs/r_analysis.yaml).
- **Pipelines:** the RNA-seq and ChIP/ATAC pipelines were run end to end on simulated data, and
  their results matched the simulated truth. The Hi-C, scRNA-seq and consensus-genome pipelines are
  dry-run tested. Every pipeline's conda environment has been built from its file. Full runs on real
  data are planned.
- **Facts and thresholds:** QC thresholds were checked against ENCODE's published standards, tool
  options against each tool's own documentation or source code, and references against PubMed.

Found a mistake? Please use the "Report an issue" link at the bottom of any page.

## Example study

Several guides illustrate results with an openly available study of primate astrocyte evolution:

> Ciuba K, Piotrowska A, Chaudhury D, *et al.* Molecular signature of primate astrocytes reveals
> pathways and regulatory changes contributing to human brain evolution. *Cell Stem Cell*
> 2025;32:426–444. [doi:10.1016/j.stem.2024.12.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.stem.2024.12.011)
